{{Short description|Dutch mathematician (1797–1866)}}
[[File:RehuelLabatto.jpg|thumb|Rehuel Lobatto]]
[[File:Delft34.JPG|thumb|Plaque in Delft]]
'''Rehuel Lobatto''' (6 June 1797 &ndash; 9 February 1866 <ref name="jewishencyclopedia.com"/> ) was a [[Dutch people|Dutch]] [[mathematician]]. 
The [[Gaussian quadrature#Gauss–Lobatto rules|Gauss-Lobatto quadrature method]] is named after him, as are [[List_of_Runge–Kutta_methods#Lobatto_methods|his variants]] on the [[Runge–Kutta methods]] for solving [[ordinary differential equation|ODEs]], and the [[Orthogonal polynomials|Lobatto polynomials]]. <ref>See: John Burkardt (ND). [https://people.sc.fsu.edu/~jburkardt/c_src/lobatto_polynomial/lobatto_polynomial.html "Lobatto polynomial"]. [[Florida State University]]</ref>
He was the author of a great number [[:nl:Rehuel_Lobatto#Publicaties|of articles]] in scientific periodicals, as well as various schoolbooks. 

Lobatto was born in [[Amsterdam]] to a [[Sephardic Jews in the Netherlands|Portuguese Jewish]] family. 
As a schoolboy Lobatto already displayed remarkable talent for mathematics.
<ref name="jewishencyclopedia.com"> Gotthard Deutsch, E. Slijper (1906). [http://www.jewishencyclopedia.com/view.jsp?artid=506&letter=L "LOBATTO, REHUEL"], ''[[The Jewish Encyclopedia]]''.</ref>  
He studied mathematics under [[Jean Henri van Swinden]] at the [[Athenaeum Illustre of Amsterdam]], earning his [[Bachelor of Arts|BA]] in 1812; <ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=144900}}</ref> and then with [[Adolphe Quetelet]] (coediting a volume of [https://books.google.com/books?id=ndhSAAAAcAAJ "Correspondance Mathématique et Physique"]).

Working for the Dutch government - initially for the [[Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations|Ministry of the Interior]] - he became secretary of a statistical commission in 1831.<ref>
{{Cite book
| publisher = Springer
| isbn = 90-247-0518-5
| last = Butter
| first = Irene Hasenberg
| title = Academic economics in Holland 1800&ndash;1870
| date = 1970-07-31
}}</ref>
From 1826 till 1849 he was editor of the ''[[:Nl: Jaarboekje_van_Lobatto|"Jaarboekje van Lobatto"]]'', as those editions of the [[:Nl:Statistisch jaarboek voor het Koningrijk der Nederlanden|official annual of statistics]] came to be known. 
In 1841 he was appointed by Minister [[Jan Jacob Rochussen|Rochussen]] as a member of a commission for the conversion of the public debt. 
In 1842 he was appointed Professor <ref>[[:Nl: Hoogleraar|"Hoogleraar"]]; see [[Academic ranks in the Netherlands]].</ref> of Higher Mathematics <ref name="knaw"/> at the [[Polytechnical School of Delft]], remaining there until his final years.

In 1836 he became member of the Royal Institute, predecessor of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref name="knaw">{{cite web|author= |url=https://dwc.knaw.nl/?s=Rehuel+Lobatto |title=Rehuel Lobatto (1797 - 1866) |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |accessdate=30 March 2022}}</ref> 
The [[Order of the Netherlands Lion]] was conferred upon him; he received his Doctoral degree ''[[honoris causa]]'' from [[Groningen University]]. <ref name="jewishencyclopedia.com"/>
